title: Booking API in Express
idea: The booking API exposes holds and bookings as REST resources, with each layer doing one job: controller validates, service decides inside a transaction, repository runs SQL.

analogy.text: A restaurant pass. The waiter checks the order is readable, the chef decides how to cook it, and the pantry only fetches ingredients.
analogy.breaks: A kitchen can improvise; the repository never makes decisions.

points: Holding seats is `POST /shows/:showId/holds`; it returns 201 or 409.
Booking is `POST /bookings` with an Idempotency-Key header; replays return 200.
`zod` rejects bad bodies with 400 before the service runs.
One error middleware maps domain errors to HTTP status codes.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. Payment is left out: charge before calling `book`, outside the transaction.

walk.text: Schema for the demo: seat rows per show and bookings with a unique Idempotency-Key.
A fixed demo clock keeps output stable; `tx` gives each service call one transaction.
Repository: lock free seats in order, then mark them HELD for ten minutes.
Service `hold`: 404 for an unknown show, 409 when any seat is taken, else `heldUntil`.
Service `book`: replay a known key; otherwise book the live hold (payment happens before this).
Controllers parse with `zod` and demand the key; Express 5 forwards async throws to the error middleware.
Error middleware maps validation, domain, duplicate-key and unknown errors to status codes.

pitfalls: Never call the payment provider inside an open database transaction; locks stay held while you wait.
Two requests with one new key can both miss the lookup; UNIQUE must catch it.
Do not return 500 for a taken seat; 409 tells the client to refresh the map.

quiz.q: What status does the second identical POST /bookings print?
quiz.why: The service finds a booking stored under Idempotency-Key k-1 and returns it unchanged. The controller marks a replay with 200.

takeaway: Validate in the controller, decide in a transaction, retry safely with Idempotency-Key.

starters: Where should the payment call go if not inside the transaction?
How do I return 409 when two requests share one new Idempotency-Key?
Should holds be their own table instead of columns on show_seat?
